summary:
Fixer D (M3 fix round 2) is done in the working tree, with nothing committed. D1 and D2 are adopted in a corrected form; D3 is text plus measurements; D4's tests are in; D5's goldens are re-blessed and every value move is explained. The final `scripts/verify` gives 735 pass and 1 fail. The only failure is T-PERF-01's timing, worst valid 8 at 61.47 ms against the 60 ms guard, with the machine 10–40 % busy (median 23 %). The tree before this round also fails T-PERF-01 under the same load (60.97 ms), so the failure is the load, not this round.

**D1: hidden gaps crossed at a slant.** V1's two-sided distance rule does not pass the lead's own check. It merges a corner or an edge next to a face where the verdict shows the faces:
- a rod's edge over a plate: 32–41 of 9,600 lines;
- a roof of two plates edge to edge: 9–44 lines, even with the plates 0.013 apart;
- on the plausible set, 4,164 of its 5,207 joins; 65 designs moved, 4 of them a tier;
- worst valid 4 dropped from Hard to Normal.

So the merge test is now the measure's own hide test at the two points where the line leaves one part and enters the next (`Edge.hiddenGap`). Each face's probe sits `HIDE_OFFSET` along its normal and must lie within `EPS_GEOM` of the other part. Thinness' union chord and the edge's thickness both use it.
- Plates turned 0–75° about the blade's length and across it: Thinness only jumps where SurfaceComplexity says the faces show.
- V1's turned laminate now reads 0.3017 / 0.3021 / 0.3033, and the diagonal Wedge split no longer jumps at 0.0113.
- Moves: no F, C, X or A value moves. Worst valid 4, 8, 9 and 10 move only in their last digits. 14 ribbed-bar plausible designs move, with no tier change.
- Gate: Analyze.run against the tree before, alternating in one process, 41 rounds, gives ratios 0.995–1.028. Worst valid 8 is ×1.0255, which projects to 54.8 ms quiet, under 57.

**D2: face ties.** The lead's first option, a fixed nudge of the line, passes the gates. But it decides each tie by its direction: a groove's two edges go opposite ways, and it moves 1,270 plausible designs, 82 of them a tier. I took the lead's second option instead, an exact tie rule inside Factors: every part except the probe's own is read grown by `TIE` = 1e-10, in both the box test and `Shapes.chord`'s existing dilation. This makes Shapes' own rule that a face belongs to its part robust to rounding. Shapes itself is unchanged.
- Y draws on six seeds: G moves on no design (53 of 3,000 before), and Thinness only in its last bits (≤ 1.14e-14).
- Blocks written another way: G moves on none.
- 544 shifted copies of the Parity fixtures: G moves on none along Y (45 before).
- `tests/Physics` without T-PERF-01 passes 339/339 on each of the six seeds.
- What it moved:
  - four X04/X05 fixtures, Hammering 0.1044 → 0.1037 (F5's value);
  - 5 generated designs;
  - 850 plausible designs, 53 of them a played tier.

  Every probe whose thickness changed lies on another part's face, so these are all face ties.

**D3: aimed re-cuts.**
- V1's aimed plate: 0.1075 Normal whole, 0.2141 Hard in 6 pieces, 0.3254 in 11.
- A re-cut that lowers G: 0.2158 Hard whole → 0.1446 Normal in 4 pieces → 0.0024 in 11.
- V2's Wedge re-cuts: G changes by up to 0.0521, with a tier on 2 designs.
- O11's options are costed: (ii) the floor of 8 probes is measured on a scratch variant, not adopted; (iii) the solid-following grid is described, not built.

**D4.**
- FA8, `TIE` = 0, V1's rule and a no-merge mutant are each killed by a new test.
- V1's slanted case fails on the tree before.
- FA2 on its own now survives: the hidden-gap test also merges a gap at the window's edge. Its case kills FA2 together with the hidden-gap test's `EPS_GEOM` dropped, and kills FA2 alone on the tree before.

**D5.** Only the 5 difficulty and parity goldens changed. SPEC, E-S2.13, both module headers and my M3-notes section are updated.

deviations: D1: the merge test is the measure's own hide test at the two crossing points, not V1's two-sided distance test. V1's test fails the lead's own check: it merges a corner or an edge next to a face where the verdict shows the faces. On every facing gap tried the two agree. The cheaper form (the plain closure, then the nearest chord past each end) gives the same chords as V1's closure on every corpus.

D2: I used the lead's second option, an exact tie rule inside Factors (every other part grown by TIE = 1e-10, a closed rule), not the world-vector nudge. The nudge passed the same gates but decides each tie by its direction (a groove's two edges go opposite ways, and an X mirror swaps them) and moved 1,270 plausible designs and 82 tiers, against 850 and 53.

D2 tests assert Thinness within 1e-12, not to the bit. Under a Y draw or another writing its last bits follow the rounding of L and of the chords (≤ 1.14e-14 on about a third of the steps), so 'to the bit' cannot hold.

D4: FA2 on its own is now equivalent on laminates, because the hidden-gap test merges a gap at the window's edge with its own EPS_GEOM. Its case kills FA2 on the tree before, and FA2 together with the hidden-gap test's EPS_GEOM dropped on this tree.

The fix-round-1 laminate case now holds Thinness within 1e-9 instead of 1e-12: a chord that ends on another part's slanted face is read TIE/cos longer.

Any rule that removes rounding's say moves about that many (the nudge moved 1,270). Closed is Shapes.chord's own rule.

The 57 ms gate rests on a projection from loaded, alternating runs (54.8 ms for worst valid 8). No quiet T-PERF-01 has been run on this tree. Under this machine's ordinary load T-PERF-01 fails at about 60–62 ms, and so does the tree before.
